profile.onboarding: First stages are wide and flat with minimal instruction, easing players into the tilt control before adding hazards.
profile.controls: One stick tilts the whole world; there are no separate jump/action buttons in the core mode.
profile.core_loop: Roll the ball across a floating stage to reach the goal gate before the timer runs out.
profile.goals_and_rewards: Reaching the goal gate triggers a celebration; bananas scattered along the route are the main collectible reward.
profile.difficulty_curve: Ramps steadily across worlds, with later stages demanding precise, fast tilting.
profile.game_feel: Praised for excellent ball physics and camera work, giving strong tactile feedback on every roll and near-miss.
profile.art_and_audio: Bright, cheerful low-poly worlds with an energetic announcer voice on key moments.
profile.session_length: About 30-60 seconds per stage, so sessions are made of many quick attempts.
profile.usability: Falling off restarts the stage almost instantly, keeping frustration low despite failure.
profile.accessibility: Every stage has a hard timer, and fine tilt control becomes demanding in later worlds, which may frustrate the youngest players.
profile.ads_and_purchases: None in the main packaged releases; some mobile spin-off versions differ and weren't checked here.
profile.notes: Good benchmark for whether Rolly Bally's fall-and-respawn (no timer) is a gentler, more 5-7-friendly version of this same fall-out mechanic.
